question: I am an incoming MS student registering for my first semester. What should I do to start planning my program?
answer: Here is our recommended game plan: Review the general MS program description & requirements at http://www.cs.columbia.edu/education/ms/ . Choose your MS Pathway on MICE . (MICE accounts will be created for incoming Fall students in June or July and for incoming Spring students in January) Plan to take your fundamental and elective courses for your chosen pathway. Identify any previously taken courses you can import to substitute for “fundamental courses”. Keep track of your progress through Stellic , your MICE account, and your degree progress checklist .

question: What are the overall requirements of the program?
answer: You must complete a total of 30 or more graduate credit points at Columbia while maintaining a minimum grade point average of 2.7. You must also complete the Columbia Engineering Professional Development & Leadership (PDL) requirement, s atisfy breadth requirements , and take at least 6 points of technical courses at the 6000 level. The CSMS program is designed to take 3 semesters to complete. If you have questions or concerns about completing the degree requirements within this timeframe, please speak with your CS Faculty Advisor or CS Advising.

question: What are my program options?
answer: You should select a concentration in a field of your interest. The department offers the following pathways: Computational Biology Computer Security Foundations of Computer Science Machine Learning Natural Language Processing Network Systems Software Systems Vision and Graphics Each pathway has its own set of standards and choice of elective courses. There is also the option of designing a Personalized or MS Thesis . If you are interested in the Personalized or MS Thesis Pathway, please contact CS Advising .

question: What is a personalized pathway?
answer: This pathway allows you to develop a specialized program not covered in the standard pathways described above. If interested in this pathway, please contact CS Advising . You must find an advisor who agrees to supervise your program, and then you develop your own customized MS program with your advisor.

question: Can I write a thesis?
answer: Yes. If you want to write a thesis, you can select the MS Thesis . Like the Personalized pathway, you will need to find a faculty thesis advisor and develop your program with him/her. The thesis pathway should include the 12-point breadth requirement, 9 points of thesis (E6902), and 9 points of other graduate CS courses selected with your advisor. A thesis proposal should be presented to your thesis committee at least three months before your defense, and a publication-quality thesis document is published as a CS department technical report.

question: When and how do I select a pathway?
answer: Please select your pathway, called a “track” in MICE . You are required to select a pathway as soon as your MICE account is created. (MICE accounts will be created for incoming Fall students in June or July and for incoming Spring students in January) If you want to change your pathway later, you can do so up until the beginning of your second semester. If you are an international student, please keep in mind that the request to change your pathway after the beginning of the second semester may not be granted. This rule applies to all pathways including personalized and thesis pathways.

question: Who is my CS Faculty Advisor?
answer: Each pathway has one or two faculty advisors . You will be assigned an advisor after you choose a pathways on MICE.

question: How many non-CS/non-pathway courses can I take as part of the program?
answer: Up to 3 points of advisor-approved CU graduate courses can be included. To qualify, the course must be relevant to the CS MS pathway and technical in nature. Please submit the course syllabus to your CS Faculty Advisor for review, and then forward the approval confirmation email to ms-advising@cs.columbia.edu

question: How many project and research credits (E6901/ E6902 and research credits from other departments) can I include in my 30 required credits?
answer: All MS students can take a maximum of 12 project/research points, 9 of which can be thesis points if you are in the MS Thesis pathway. Current AMR students will be registered by SEAS to be at full time status. It is NOT permitted to take COMS 6901 in addition to AMR credits.

question: Can I waive a Breadth Requirement?
answer: Breadth may only be waived if you took the course at Columbia. If you received Advanced Standing credit for the course in question, you will also earn credits towards your CS MS. Otherwise, you must replace the waived course with another COMS course (4000 or higher) to reach the required total of 30 credits. Please email ms-advising@cs.columbia.edu for more information on the Advanced Standing application process.

question: I am a US citizen. Can I be a part-time student?
answer: Yes but you must register for at least 3 points each semester.

question: How can I find out which courses are offered this Fall and Spring semesters?
answer: Vergil has the most up-to-date information. As not every course is offered every semester, we recommend using Vergil to look at past semesters to determine whether a specific course is likely to be offered. You can also ask the instructor of that course when they plan to offer it again.

question: I want to drop a course after the Change of Program period. Is that possible?
answer: It is possible to drop a course via the Vergil Appeals process up until the last day your school permits this. Please keep in mind that even though it is possible to drop a course, there are no refunds after the Change of Program. If you want to avoid financial penalties, please finalize your schedule during the regular registration period or the Change of Program Period. If you are an international student, you may not be able to drop a course due to the full-time registration requirement. Please consult ms-advising@cs.columbia.edu .

question: I want to do research/project with a faculty. Should I register for COMS W4901 or COMS E6901?
answer: Working with CS Faculty: You can obtain registration information(call and section number) from the faculty you are working with. Please add yourself to the waitlist and the faculty will need to approve you to be added to the course. If you or the faculty are unsure about the registration details, please email ms-advising@cs.columbia.edu for assistance. Working with Non-CS Faculty: Students may work with faculty to identify a course in the respective department that is equivalent to COMS E6901 and follow that department’s registration process. Please note that approval from your faculty advisor is required for any non-CS course to count toward the CSMS program as a secondary elective or a non-CS course elective. It is strongly recommended to seek approval before registering for any non-CS courses.

question: Can I take on-campus courses in the summer as a CVN student?
answer: If the course that you want to take is offered, you are allowed to register for it with permission from the instructor, and after completing an on-campus petition ( Change of Status Request )

question: I am an on-campus student, can I take a CVN course?
answer: CVN course petitions are only permitted if the course is not offered in person or the student is in their last semester, needing accommodation to complete the program requirements. On-campus students are expected to take in-person classes. Petitions can be submitted to ( Change of Status Request )

question: Do I need prerequisites?
answer: The registration system does not enforce prerequisites. Published prerequisites list specific Columbia undergraduate courses – instructors expect that you have covered material from those courses. If you are a transfer student or graduate student, we do not expect that you took those specific courses at Columbia, only that you are academically prepared to successfully pass the course. Graduate students (MS and Doctoral) should not register for 3000-level courses. These will not count towards your CS MS. If you doubt you are prepared for a particular course, please speak to the instructor and talk to CS Advising .

question: Can I transfer graduate credits for courses taken at another university?
answer: No, but you can waive courses from your pathway’s “fundamental courses” section if you have taken similar courses at another institution. For the waiver to be approved, the previous course must be equivalent to what we offer here at Columbia, and the grade you received must be B or higher. Waiver requests are submitted through MICE. Forms are electronically transferred to the relevant course instructors for approval, and you will be notified by email of their decisions. If approved, you still have to complete a minimum of 30 credit hours to receive your degree, but you can take other CS courses in place of the waived requirements. Note that class imports must be completed during your first semester only. Go to MICE → Students menu → Course Imports → Add Course Import → Upload the necessary transcript and syllabus

question: Can I transfer graduate credits for courses taken at Columbia?
answer: Yes. Please see the SEAS policy on Advanced Standing on their website. To apply for Advanced Standing, please fill out an Advanced Standing Form. Advanced Standing towards the MS degree must be from 4000-level courses or above, taken at Columbia University only for any passing grade, and cannot have been counted towards a previous degree. No more than 15 points of Advanced Standing are awarded, and the grades from the advanced standing points will not be counted into your overall MS program GPA, which should be 2.7 or higher. Appropriate confirmation from your undergraduate program and school is required. Detailed advanced standing instructions can be found here .

question: I've taken some core courses here at Columbia, but I had to use them for my undergraduate degree. What should I do?
answer: If you used these courses toward your undergraduate degree, you cannot transfer credits, but you may be able to waive these and replace the credits with alternative courses. For more information, please contact ms-advising@cs.columbia.edu .

question: How many CVN courses can I take as an on-campus MS student?
answer: You must be a CVN student to access the online lectures. CVN course petitions are explained above.

question: I need to take a temporary leave from the program, can I do this?
answer: If you have completed at least one full semester in the program, are in good academic standing with a GPA of 2.7 or higher, and will not be away from the program for more than a total of 12 months, then you are eligible to apply for a Leave of Absence. Fill out a Change of Status form and select the Leave of Absence request type. This will be reviewed by both the department and the SEAS Office of Graduate Student Services. If you fail to return from your absence, you will be withdrawn from the program. Contact CS advising to discuss this further.

question: I have just enrolled as a Masters student this semester. Can I take a Leave of Absence immediately?
answer: No, you can only take a Leave of Absence if you have been in the program for one full semester. If you have to leave before this time, you will need to officially withdraw from the program and reapply for admission. Your online application and official documents are held for at least 12 months from your original submission date and can be reactivated within this time.

question: I have been out of the M.S. program without an approved Leave of Absence, can I rejoin the program?
answer: You can apply for readmission using the Readmission to Graduate Program application form. Authorization for readmission is at the discretion of the CS department.

question: What do I need to do in order to graduate?
answer: You need to complete the following steps: Complete the Application for Degree . Deadline dates for filing the application are listed here . Complete the CSMS Checklist Review and OPT Request form to verify your CSMS degree progress. If you are an international student, you can also upload your OPT form, and CS Advising can complete the academic portion of the form for you.

question: When do I need to complete graduation paperwork by?
answer: Deadline dates for filing the application are listed here .

question: What is the process of graduation clearance?
answer: Once your paperwork has been filed, your Application for Degree is processed by the Registrar. Your official transcript gets forwarded to the CS department and is reviewed. Following this review, you will be notified whether or not you have been cleared for graduation at the department level. Your record is then forwarded to SEAS and Columbia for further review. Be warned that although you may satisfy the department MS requirements, you may still be blocked from graduation by any outstanding holds or requirements not yet met at the university level.

question: It is the beginning of a new semester, and I have fulfilled all of the requirements for my MS degree last semester, but I have yet to apply for graduation. Do I need to register as a student to do this?
answer: You do not need to register, but you do need to fill out the Application for Degree as soon as possible. Also, please complete the other steps outlined above.

question: I am applying for the post-completion Optional Practical Training as part of my F1 VISA. How do I get my OPT approval form signed?
answer: Please email ms-advising@cs.columbia.edu.

question: I failed a requirement in my final semester. What can I do?
answer: Please make sure that you monitor your grades throughout the semester to avoid this happening. You may count 1 D grade towards your CSMS. If you have an F for a course you need for a CS MS Requirement or credits, you will not be able to graduate. You must complete the remaining requirement(s) in the following semester. Please note that it is not possible to extend your program with ISSO or COMS to do this. The failed requirement must be completed via petition for a CVN course or via OPT for international students. Remember that your home country may have rules on degree verification for online coursework; you must make an informed decision on how to proceed. Students without visa requirements should also complete via CVN. All students will be required to submit a completion plan and may need to petition additionally to SEAS to make up the failed coursework/credits.

question: How can I request a certification letter confirming program completion before my degree is conferred?
answer: You can request a certification letter by submitting a SEAS Certification Letter Request . The request can be found under “Letter Request”
